newsitem.title: USA: Harken says 'too early' to peg Colombia reserves.
newsitem.headline: Harken says 'too early' to peg Colombia reserves.

text.p: Harken Energy Corp Chairman Mike Faulkner on Thursday said it is "too early in the process" to estimate total oil reserves from its Bolivar contract in Colombia.

Faulkner declined to confirm or deny published reports the 250,000 acre Magdalena Basin tract covered under its Bolivar association contract could hold more than 1.0 billion barrels of recoverable crude oil reserves.
"To assign any reserves, it's too early in the process," he said as the company prepared to drill the first in a series of exploratory wells beginning in August.

Fulkner reaffirmed June estimates of between 30,000 and 100,000 barrels per acre of oil in place in the 250,000 acre concession. The company estimated 10 percent to 20 percent of the oil, or 3,000 to 20,000 barrels per acre, could be recoverable.

The Irving, Texas-based independent oil company budgeted $20 million to drill three horizontal wells. Initial results from the first well -- Catalina 1 -- should be available 30 days after the well is spudded in August, Faulkner said.

The initial well will be drilled horizontally to test a geological feature first drilled with a vertical well by Esso in the 1950s. More than 500,000 barrels of oil averaging better than 35 degrees specific gravity were produced.

In similar vertically fractured wells in the Austin Chalk region of east Texas, horizontal wells have recovered an average 16.7 times more oil than was recovered by earlier vertical wells in the same trend, the company said.
The 4,000-acre area to be tested by the Catalina 1 well holds the potential to recover 12 million to 80 million barrels, the company said in the June announcement.
"We're bringing 1990s technology to an area that has literally been overlooked for more than 40 years," Faulkner said.
